answer: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1 establish continuing responsibility despite outsourcing; they do not supply a complete test of fulfillment. A justified conclusion would require an applicable legal standard and evidence connecting retained authority, actual supervision, and operational and ownership-record outcomes to that standard over the relevant period. Contractual allocation, a supervision log, or a completed reconciliation alone does not establish fulfillment. No entity-specific conclusion is possible on the supplied facts.

claims.inference: Text: outsourcing does not remove the Product Provider’s responsibility. Deduction: identifying the responsible party establishes allocation of responsibility, not satisfactory performance.
missing_premises: Applicability of the retained edition to the product, activity and assessment period, including relevant conditions or modifications.
The assessed entity’s Product Provider role.
claims.proposition: Ultimate responsibility continues despite delegation of functions.
claims.status: Supported by express text; actual applicability unresolved

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds.

claims.inference: Evaluative proposal: contracts, governance arrangements and enforceable information, intervention and remediation rights could evidence retained authority. Their actual availability and use would matter. The cited text does not prescribe these items as a sufficient checklist.
missing_premises: An applicable standard specifying what authority and control retention requires.
Actual contracts, governance arrangements, delegated functions and practical ability to direct or remedy outsourced performance.
claims.proposition: Allocation of authority is relevant evidence of retained responsibility, but a contractual reservation alone does not establish fulfillment.
claims.status: Reasoned evidential proposal, not an express discharge test

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.
For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

claims.inference: Deduction: a recorded supervisory event establishes, at most, evidence of an activity; adequacy depends on its substance, scope, timing and follow-up. UT 6.11C supplies an express conduct standard for valuation outsourcing, but transferring that standard to all tokenisation supervision requires a separate applicability argument.
missing_premises: The applicable supervisory standard and its relationship to paragraph 10.
Evidence of competent review, risk coverage, frequency, findings, escalation and remediation throughout the assessment period.
For direct reliance on UT 6.11C, management-company status and valuation outsourcing within its scope.
claims.proposition: Supervisory conduct must be assessed for adequacy; its mere occurrence is insufficient.
claims.status: Supported distinction; standard and factual application unresolved

support.quote: Where a third party is engaged in the valuation of a scheme, the management company shall exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in the selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring of such third party
The valuation activities of such third party should be subject to ongoing supervision and periodic review by the management company.
robust and properly maintained policies and procedures, systems and controls underpinning the operation of the Tokenised Securities

claims.inference: Text: operational soundness and ownership record keeping are substantive subjects of responsibility; paragraph 11 separately requires proper records and compatibility. Deduction: reconciliation completion does not establish that records correctly reflect legally valid interests or that discrepancies were resolved. Evaluative proposal: examine record accuracy and completeness, legal entitlement mapping, reconciliation results, exceptions and operational performance against an applicable standard.
missing_premises: Applicable criteria for operational soundness, proper records and compatibility, including relevant timing and tolerances.
The legally effective ownership and settlement arrangements.
Actual records, reconciliation coverage and results, unresolved discrepancies, incidents and corrective action.
A justified rule connecting this evidence to fulfillment of paragraph 10 rather than only paragraph 11 or an individual control.
claims.proposition: Operational and record-keeping outcomes require substantive verification; successful process execution is not a sufficient compliance conclusion.

support.quote: Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

whether the ownership interest of the underlying assets of the Tokenised Securities are legally valid under the applicable governing laws, whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens, or whether any encumbrance affects the extrinsic rights.

rival_readings: Allocation reading: paragraph 10 principally preserves ultimate accountability despite outsourcing, while other provisions specify performance requirements. This supports retained responsibility but does not make contractual allocation sufficient for overall compliance.

Substantive reading: responsibility for management, operational soundness and ownership record keeping requires effective conduct and satisfactory performance, not merely nominal accountability. The text does not define a complete adequacy threshold.
Combined reading: authority, supervisory conduct and outcomes should be considered together. This is a proposed assessment approach, not an express statutory checklist or established sufficient test.
unresolved: The retained text does not resolve whether paragraph 10 imposes a particular conduct standard, an outcome standard, or a combination, nor how an operational failure affects fulfillment.
The Appendix supplies non-exhaustive factors where applicable; it does not establish a universal safe harbour.
Actual authority, supervision and outcomes are not supplied. Neither fulfillment nor breach can be concluded.
A model or solver accepting the candidate rule establishes neither the interpretation’s legal correctness nor the Product Provider’s fulfillment.
